test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 26th July 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

She speaks / very highly / of both her / daughter-in-laws.
solution:
The correct answer is **'daughter-in-laws'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'daughters-in-law'** should be used instead of **'daughter-in-laws'.**
 
• Some **hyphenated** terms are made up of a **noun** and some other parts of speech. For example, *'passer-by'* is made up of a noun (passer) and a preposition (by). *'Secretary-general'* contains a **noun** (secretary) and an **adjective** (general).
 
• With these terms, you should **pluralize** only the nou
